trial_court: Sessions Judge/Addl DC (Judicial), East Jaintia Hills District, Khliehriat, Sessions Case No.68 of 2021
case_name: Shri Phot Khaii vs The State Of Meghalaya

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Meghalaya, represented by the Secretary, Home Department, Government of Meghalaya, Shillong; The Superintendent of Police, East Jaintia Hills District, Meghalaya; The Officer-in charge, Khliehriat Police Station, East Jaintia Hills District, Meghalaya — prosecution

facts_of_case: The Appellant was convicted by the Trial Court for the offence under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to undergo Rigorous Life Imprisonment with a fine of Rs.50,000/-in default to undergo Simple Imprisonment for 5 months. The case involved the murder of Oli Siangshai by the Appellant.

legal_principles.principle: The prosecution should not be allowed to become a persecution.
legal_principles.held: However, inordinately long delay may be taken as presumptive proof of prejudice.
cited_cases: Shri Phot Khaii vs The State Of Meghalaya, (2024)

legal_principles.principle: An accused's plea of denial of speedy trial cannot be defeated by saying that the accused did not demand a speedy trial.
legal_principles.held: If in a given case, he did make such a demand and yet he was not tried speedily, it would be a plus point in his favour, but the mere non-asking for a speedy trial cannot be put against the accused.
cited_cases: Shri Phot Khaii vs The State Of Meghalaya, (2024)

legal_principles.principle: The court has to balance and weigh the several relevant factors - 'balancing test' or 'balancing process' - and determine in each case whether the right to speedy trial has been denied.
legal_principles.held: Ultimately, the court has to balance and weigh the several relevant factors - 'balancing test' or 'balancing process' - and determine in each case whether the right to speedy trial has been denied.
cited_cases: Shri Phot Khaii vs The State Of Meghalaya, (2024)

legal_principles.principle: The prosecution has to justify and explain the delay in a complaint of denial of right to speedy trial.
legal_principles.held: In every case of complaint of denial of right to speedy trial, it is primarily for the prosecution to justify and explain the delay.
cited_cases: Shri Phot Khaii vs The State Of Meghalaya, (2024)

outcome.final_order: The Appellant's conviction and sentence were upheld, but the period already undergone in prison was ordered to be set off.
